content.title: About
content.content: Turkey heart is a muscular offal with a dense, springy texture and a rich meaty flavor. It is larger than a chicken heart and very lean. Turkey hearts are braised, boiled, fried, cooked on skewers, and added to stews, soups, and ground meat.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: A turkey heart is noticeably larger than a chicken heart.
It is a muscle, so it needs either long braising or thin slicing.
Turkey heart is one of the leanest offal cuts.
Before cooking, fat, vessels, and blood clots are trimmed off.
Turkey hearts are braised for about thirty to forty minutes to become tender.

items.title: Source of protein
items.content: Turkey heart provides high-quality protein with modest fat.

items.title: Contains iron
items.content: Iron is well absorbed and is needed for oxygen transport.

items.title: Contains vitamin B12
items.content: Vitamin B12 is important for the nervous system and the formation of blood cells.

items.title: Contains zinc and selenium
items.content: These nutrients support immunity and cell protection.

items.title: Contains coenzyme Q10
items.content: Coenzyme Q10 helps cells produce energy.

items.title: Cholesterol
items.content: Offal contains cholesterol, so people with high cholesterol should limit portions.

items.title: Gout
items.content: Hearts contain purines, which may trigger gout attacks.

items.title: Undercooked meat
items.content: Undercooked hearts may contain Salmonella and Campylobacter; they should be cooked until fully done.

items.title: Fat and salt when cooked
items.content: Grilling with a marinade or frying in breading adds a lot of fat and salt to the dish.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Rinse the hearts, trim off the fat, vessels, and blood clots, and slice. Braise them with sour cream and onion for about 30–40 minutes until tender, fry them, thread on skewers and grill, or add to stews and soups. Cook until fully done.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store raw hearts in the refrigerator in a covered container for one to two days or freeze them. Thaw in the refrigerator. Keep cooked hearts in the refrigerator for three to four days.
